task.title: rle-encode
task.statement: The rle package exposes decode (already implemented) and a stub encode(s). Implement encode(s) so that it run-length encodes a string: each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run (the count is always written, even when it is 1). For example encode('aaabbc') is 'a3b2c1', encode('abc') is 'a1b1c1', encode('') is ''. encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x). Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change decode or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: TypeError when s is not a string

spec.infeasibility_reason: The required encoding format cannot round-trip every string with the unchanged decode. For example, encode('a1') must produce 'a111': 'a1' for the run of 'a', followed by '11' for the run of '1'. The existing decode greedily consumes all following digits as the count, so decode('a111') returns 111 copies of 'a', not 'a1'. Satisfying all requirements requires either restricting the input domain or changing the encoding format and decoder.
spec.restated_task: Implement encode(s), publicly available from rle, to return a str containing each maximal run's character followed by its decimal length, including lengths of one and multi-digit lengths; return an empty string for empty input and raise TypeError for non-string input. Preserve decode and existing tests. The additional requirement to round-trip every string contradicts this format and the existing decoder.

interface_contract.name: encode
interface_contract.behavior: Accept str inputs, including str subclasses. Process characters as Python string elements, preserving their order without normalization. For each maximal consecutive run, append its character and its positive count in ordinary decimal digits without leading zeros. Return a str; empty input returns ''. The requested universal round-trip guarantee is infeasible.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str.

interface_contract.name: decode
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation: read one character, greedily consume subsequent characters satisfying isdigit() as its count, convert that count with int(), repeat the character accordingly, and concatenate the results. Empty input returns ''.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str.
ValueError: a parsed character has no following count digits.
ValueError: a consumed count cannot be converted by int(), including certain Unicode characters accepted by isdigit().

acceptance_criteria: 5. encode('aabaa') == 'a2b1a2', preserving separate runs of the same character.
7. Every successful encode call returns an instance of str, including calls with empty input or a str subclass.
8. Non-string inputs, including None, 123, b'abc', and ['a'], raise TypeError.
10. The requested guarantee decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x is unsatisfiable: criterion 9 and the unchanged decoder imply decode(encode('a1')) == 'a' * 111.
11. Preserve decode unchanged, including decode('a3b1') == 'aaab', decode('') == '', and TypeError for decode(123).
12. Preserve existing test files and the public imports from rle.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception raised in the code under test is never overridden (only a test-internal crash or a timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
